faq.title: FAQ
faq.a1: Site Mechanic is a set of website diagnostics modules (Speed & UX, SEO, Accessibility, Security, Fonts & Design, Hosting, and more). Paste a URL, run a scan, and get prioritized issues. If you need a shareable outcome, you can unlock a report with recommendations and fixes.
faq.q2: Do I need an account to run scans?
faq.a2: No. Most scans can be run without signing in. If you choose to unlock a paid report or export, you may be prompted to sign in so we can associate the purchase with your account.
faq.a3: Quick scans are typically under a minute; Lighthouse audits can take a few minutes. If a site is slow or blocks automation, scans can take longer or fail.
faq.a4: A paid report is an export/share outcome for a specific scan, such as PDF export, share links, downloadable data, or extended fix guidance. You can usually run the scan for free and then decide whether to purchase the report.
faq.a5: Credits unlock paid reports for individual scans. When a report is locked, you'll see options to buy a single report or buy a credit pack. If you already have credits, you can unlock with 1 credit.
faq.q6: The scan is stuck. What should I do?
faq.a6: Try a simpler URL (homepage vs. deep route) and re-run. If the issue persists, email peter@sitemechanic.io with the URL and module name so we can reproduce.

sectionIntros.overview: Brand consistency measures how uniformly your visual identity is applied across your website. Consistent branding builds recognition, trust, and professionalism. This overview presents your aggregate consistency score across color usage, typography, and cross-page coherence.
sectionIntros.colors: Color analysis examines your site's color palette for consistency and adherence to brand guidelines. A cohesive color palette reinforces brand identity, while excessive color variation can appear unprofessional and confuse visitors. This section identifies your dominant colors and any inconsistencies.
sectionIntros.typography: Typography analysis evaluates the font families, sizes, and styles used across your site. Consistent typography creates visual harmony and improves readability. This section identifies all typefaces in use and highlights inconsistencies in heading and body text styling.
sectionIntros.contrast: Contrast analysis evaluates the color combinations used for text and backgrounds. Sufficient contrast ensures readability for all users, including those with visual impairments. This section identifies color pairs that may fail WCAG contrast requirements.
sectionIntros.crossPage: Cross-page consistency measures how uniformly your brand elements are applied across different pages of your site. sectionIntros.metaTags: Meta tags are the foundation of how search engines and social platforms understand your page. They control how your content appears in search results, social shares, and browser tabs. This section evaluates your title tag, meta description, Open Graph, Twitter Card, viewport, and canonical URL configurations. Properly optimized meta tags can significantly improve click-through rates and prevent duplicate content issues.
sectionIntros.headings: A well-structured heading hierarchy helps both users and search engines navigate your content. Headings create a semantic outline that communicates topic relationships and content importance. This section analyzes the distribution and proper nesting of H1 through H6 tags on your page. Best practice is to have exactly one H1 tag and use subsequent levels in logical order without skipping levels.
sectionIntros.content: Content quality directly impacts search rankings and user engagement. Search engines favor pages with substantial, well-written content that thoroughly covers a topic. This section examines word count, readability, text-to-HTML ratio, and sentence structure to assess your page's content depth. Pages with fewer than 300 words are generally considered thin content and may struggle to rank competitively.
sectionIntros.images: Images enhance user experience but can hurt SEO if not properly optimized. Missing alt text reduces accessibility for screen reader users and eliminates a key ranking signal for image search. This section checks alt text coverage, image dimensions, and file references to ensure your images are accessible and search-friendly. Properly optimized images with descriptive alt attributes can drive significant traffic through Google Image Search.
sectionIntros.links: Internal and external links form the connective tissue of the web and are a primary way search engines discover and rank pages. A healthy link profile includes a strong internal linking structure that distributes page authority and helps users navigate your site. This section evaluates the balance of internal vs. external links, nofollow usage, and any broken link patterns. Broken or malformed links can waste crawl budget and create poor user experiences.
sectionIntros.mobile: With mobile-first indexing, Google prioritizes the mobile version of your site for ranking and indexing. Over 60% of web traffic now comes from mobile devices, making responsive design essential for reaching your audience. This section tests viewport configuration, font readability, tap target sizing, and horizontal scroll issues across device sizes. Pages that fail mobile usability checks may see reduced visibility in mobile search results.
sectionIntros.performance: Page speed is a confirmed ranking factor and directly affects user experience, bounce rates, and conversion rates. Studies show that a one-second delay in page load time can reduce conversions by up to 7%. This section measures load times, DOM complexity, and resource usage to identify performance bottlenecks. Optimizing these metrics improves both your Core Web Vitals scores and overall search ranking potential.
sectionIntros.security: Security signals build trust with both users and search engines, and HTTPS is a confirmed Google ranking factor. Missing security headers can leave your site vulnerable to cross-site scripting, clickjacking, and other common attacks. This section audits HTTPS status and critical security headers including HSTS, Content Security Policy, and X-Frame-Options. Implementing proper security headers protects your visitors and demonstrates technical credibility to search engines.
sectionIntros.structuredData: Structured data helps search engines understand your content and enables rich results such as star ratings, FAQs, and product cards in search results. Pages with rich results typically see 20-30% higher click-through rates compared to standard listings. This section checks for JSON-LD and Microdata markup, including the schema types implemented on your page. Google recommends JSON-LD as the preferred format for structured data implementation.
sectionIntros.additional: Beyond core SEO factors, several technical elements contribute to overall search health and user trust. A complete technical foundation includes proper browser identification, crawl directives, and tracking infrastructure. This section verifies the presence of a favicon, robots.txt, XML sitemap, analytics tracking, and social media links. Missing any of these elements can indicate an incomplete SEO setup and reduce your site's professional appearance.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the complete analysis, this section provides actionable code fixes and step-by-step implementation guides. Recommendations are organized by impact level so you can prioritize the changes that will deliver the greatest SEO improvements first. Each recommendation includes both the problematic pattern and the recommended solution with copy-ready code snippets. Implementing these fixes in order of severity will help you systematically improve your site's search performance.

description.title: Write a compelling meta description
description.description: Keep 150-160 chars, include a CTA, and ensure uniqueness.
description.missingDetail: No meta description was found. Without one, search engines pull a random snippet from your page, which often reads poorly and hurts click-through rate. A well-written description acts as ad copy for your page in search results.
description.tooShortDetail: Your description is {{len}} characters. Google displays up to ~160 characters in search results. A short description wastes this free advertising space and signals less relevance to searchers.
description.tooLongDetail: Your description is {{len}} characters and will be truncated in search results. The trailing text, which often includes a call-to-action, will be hidden behind an ellipsis.

openGraph.title: Add Open Graph & social meta tags
openGraph.impact: Rich previews on social platforms drive 2-3x more engagement
openGraph.description: When your page is shared on Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, or messaging apps, the platform looks for Open Graph and Twitter Card meta tags to build a rich preview card. Without them, shares show a plain URL or an auto-selected image that often looks wrong. Adding these tags takes minutes and dramatically improves how your content appears when shared.

images.title: Add missing image alt text
images.impact: Improves accessibility, image search rankings, and overall SEO score
images.description: {{count}} of {{total}} images are missing alt attributes. Alt text serves three purposes: it describes the image to screen-reader users (required for WCAG compliance), it appears when the image fails to load, and search engines use it to understand image content for Google Image Search rankings. Missing alt text is one of the most common SEO and accessibility issues.

headings.title: Fix heading structure
headings.impact: Clearer page structure improves crawlability and user engagement
headings.missingH1Detail: Your page is missing an H1 heading. The H1 is the primary heading that tells both search engines and users what the page is about. It carries the most weight of any heading tag and should contain your primary target keyword. Every page should have exactly one H1.
headings.multipleH1Detail: Your page has {{count}} H1 headings. Multiple H1 tags dilute the primary keyword signal and confuse search engines about the page topic. Keep one H1 as the main heading and demote others to H2 or H3.
headings.lowHeadingsDetail: Your page has very few headings ({{count}} total). Headings create a scannable outline for users and help search engines understand content hierarchy. Well-structured headings improve both readability and SEO.

content.title: Improve content depth
content.impact: Pages with 600+ words rank higher on average and earn more backlinks
content.veryThinDetail: Your page has only {{count}} words. Search engines consider this "thin content," which rarely ranks well. Pages competing in search typically have 800-2000+ words. Thin content also increases bounce rate because visitors find insufficient information and leave.
content.thinDetail: Your page has {{count}} words. While not critically thin, pages with 600+ words tend to rank better because they provide more value, answer more user questions, and naturally include more relevant keywords. Consider expanding key sections.

links.title: Fix link security & anchor text
links.impact: Prevents security vulnerabilities and improves link equity signals
links.description: External links that open in a new tab without rel="noopener noreferrer" expose your site to reverse tabnapping attacks, where the opened page can redirect your tab to a phishing site. Empty anchor text wastes link equity and provides no context to search engines or screen readers.

canonical.title: Add canonical + sitemap refs
canonical.description: Declare the preferred URL and list all discoverable URLs.
canonical.fullDescription: No canonical URL was detected. Without a canonical tag, search engines may index multiple versions of the same page (www vs non-www, HTTP vs HTTPS, with/without trailing slash) and split your ranking power between them. A canonical tag declares the single preferred URL for each page.

jsonld.title: Add JSON-LD (Article/Product)
jsonld.impact: Rich results eligibility - up to 30% more visibility
jsonld.description: Provide structured data for the primary page type.
jsonld.fullDescription: No structured data was found on this page. Structured data (JSON-LD) helps search engines understand your content type and enables rich results like star ratings, FAQ dropdowns, product prices, and breadcrumbs directly in search results. Pages with rich results get significantly higher click-through rates.

preload.title: Preload critical assets
preload.impact: Faster LCP and render - improves Core Web Vitals
preload.description: Preload hero image, main font, and critical CSS.
preload.fullDescription: Page performance scored {{score}}/100. Preloading tells the browser to fetch critical resources (hero image, fonts, CSS) as soon as possible, before it discovers them in the HTML. This can shave 200-500ms off your Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and eliminate layout shift from late-loading fonts.

defer.title: Defer non-critical JS
defer.description: Use defer for scripts that can wait until DOM is parsed.
defer.fullDescription: Synchronous scripts in the <head> block the browser from rendering any content until they finish downloading and executing. Moving non-essential scripts to defer or async allows the page to paint first, improving perceived load speed and Core Web Vitals scores (especially FID/INP).

whatIs.a: Site Mechanic is a set of website diagnostics modules (Speed & UX, SEO, Accessibility, Security, Fonts & Design, Hosting, and more). You paste a URL, run a scan, and get prioritized issues plus next-step recommendations.

accountNeeded.q: Do I need an account to run scans?
accountNeeded.a: No. Most scans can be run without signing in. If you choose a paid report/export, you may be prompted to sign in or purchase credits depending on the tool.

validUrls.a: Use a public, reachable URL (for example https://example.com). Redirects are fine. Pages behind logins or IP allow-lists may not be scannable.

scanTime.a: It depends on the module and the site. Quick scans are typically under a minute; Lighthouse audits can take a few minutes. If a site is slow or blocks automation, scans can take longer or fail.

paidReport.q: What is a "paid report" on Site Mechanic?
paidReport.a: A paid report is an export/share outcome for a specific scan, such as PDF export, share links, downloadable data, or extended fix guidance. You can usually run the scan for free and then decide whether to purchase the report.

credits.a: Credits are used to unlock paid reports for individual scans. When a report is locked, you’ll see options to buy a single report or buy a credit pack. If you already have credits, you can unlock with 1 credit.

singleReport.q: Can I buy a single report without a subscription?
singleReport.a: Yes. Many tools offer a "buy single report" option for one scan. Credit packs are also available if you run reports regularly.

refunds.a: If you’re not satisfied within the first 14 days of a subscription purchase, contact support for a refund. For one-off credit purchases, reach out and we’ll help resolve issues or correct billing mistakes.

payments.q: What payment methods do you accept?
payments.a: Payments are processed through Stripe. Most major credit/debit cards are supported. Site Mechanic does not store your full card details on our servers.

scanCount.a: A scan is when you run any analyzer (Performance, SEO, Security, etc.) on a URL. Each time you click "Analyze" or "Run Scan", it counts as one scan toward your daily limit.

reportUnlock.a: A paid report unlock gives you access to Pro features for a specific scan result: PDF export, shareable links, detailed recommendations, and saved report history. Free users can view basic scan results but need to unlock for Pro features.

planLimits.a:
Free: 10 scans per day, Pro sections are locked.
Day Pass ($20): Unlimited scans for 24 hours + 30 report unlocks.
Pro Monthly ($29/mo): Unlimited scans + 250 report unlocks per month.
Pro Annual ($290/yr): Unlimited scans + unlimited report unlocks.

dailyLimit.q: What happens when I hit my daily scan limit?
dailyLimit.a: When you reach 10 scans in a day (Free tier), the scan button is disabled until midnight UTC. You'll see upgrade options for Day Pass or Pro subscriptions to continue scanning immediately.

unlocksRunOut.q: What happens when I run out of report unlocks?
unlocksRunOut.a: For Day Pass users, you can unlock up to 30 reports during your 24-hour window. For Pro Monthly, your 250 reports reset at the start of each billing period. Pro Annual has unlimited unlocks. If you run out, you can purchase a Single Report ($5) or upgrade your plan.

dayPass.q: How does the Day Pass work?
dayPass.a: The Day Pass ($20) gives you full Pro access for 24 hours from the time of purchase. You get unlimited scans and up to 30 report unlocks during this window. It does not auto-renew—perfect for one-time projects or client presentations.

singleReport.q: How does the Single Report option work?
singleReport.a: Single Report ($5) lets you unlock one specific scan result without a subscription. After unlocking, you have permanent access to that report’s Pro features including PDF export and detailed recommendations. Great if you only need one report occasionally.

resets.a: Daily scan limits reset at midnight UTC. For Pro Monthly subscribers, report unlocks reset at the start of each billing cycle. Day Pass limits expire 24 hours after purchase.

devtoolsDiff.q: Why can results differ from what I see in Chrome DevTools?
devtoolsDiff.a: Many metrics depend on device emulation, network conditions, caching, and timing. Site Mechanic uses automated runs that may not match your exact local environment. Treat results as directional signals, then verify fixes locally.

crawlAll.q: Do you crawl my entire website?
crawlAll.a: It depends on the module. Some tools analyze a single page URL. Crawling modules (when enabled) scan multiple pages based on discovered links and limits.

localhost.q: Can you scan staging sites or localhost?
localhost.a: No. For security reasons, Site Mechanic blocks localhost and private network targets. Use a publicly reachable staging URL instead.

dataStored.q: What data is stored after I run a scan?
dataStored.a: Site Mechanic may store scan artifacts needed to generate reports (for example exported PDFs). Generated PDF files are automatically cleaned up after a retention period (7 days by default).

screenshots.a: Some reports include screenshots to make results easier to review. Screenshot/report artifacts follow the same retention approach as reports (automatic cleanup).

blockScans.a: Yes. Some sites block automated browsers, rate-limit requests, or require cookies/authentication. If a scan fails, try again, or test a different page URL.

stuck.q: The scan is stuck on a step (loading / measuring). What should I do?
stuck.a: First, try a simpler URL (homepage vs. deep route) and re-run. If the site is slow or blocks automation, the scan may time out. If the issue persists, send the URL and the module name to support so we can reproduce.

exportsLocked.q: I unlocked a report but exports are still locked.
exportsLocked.a: Refresh the page once after unlocking. If it still looks locked, the report ID may not match (for example if the scan was re-run). Re-open the same scan results page and try again, or contact support with the URL + timestamp.

sectionIntros.families: Font families define the typographic identity of your site. This section catalogs all font families detected on your page, including their weight variants, styles, and loading sources. Using too many families increases page weight and load times. Best practice is to limit your site to 2-3 font families with only the weight variants you actually use.
sectionIntros.providers: Font providers determine how fonts are delivered to your visitors. Third-party providers like Google Fonts and Adobe Fonts offer convenience but introduce external dependencies and potential privacy concerns. Self-hosting fonts gives you full control over delivery and eliminates third-party requests. This section identifies all font sources and their delivery methods.
sectionIntros.loading: Font loading speed directly impacts First Contentful Paint (FCP) and overall perceived performance. Slow-loading fonts cause invisible text (FOIT) or flash of unstyled text (FOUT), degrading user experience. This section evaluates loading time, estimated bandwidth cost, and the impact on rendering performance. Using font-display: swap and preloading critical fonts are key optimization strategies.
sectionIntros.privacy: Loading fonts from third-party CDNs sends visitor IP addresses and browsing data to external servers. Under GDPR and similar privacy regulations, this may require explicit user consent. Google Fonts has been the subject of GDPR enforcement actions in several EU countries. This section identifies privacy implications of your font loading strategy and highlights potential compliance risks.
sectionIntros.delivery: Font delivery optimization ensures fonts are downloaded efficiently. Using modern formats like WOFF2 reduces file sizes by 30-50% compared to older formats. This section analyzes font file requests, formats, sizes, and loading times. Implementing preconnect hints for external font servers and preloading critical font files accelerates delivery.
sectionIntros.stability: Layout stability during font loading prevents jarring visual shifts that frustrate users and hurt Core Web Vitals scores. Proper fallback font stacks and font-display settings minimize Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). This section analyzes your fallback stacks, font-display usage, and CLS risk factors. Using size-adjusted fallback fonts with metric overrides can virtually eliminate font-related layout shift.
sectionIntros.advanced: Advanced typography features like variable fonts, subsetting, and unicode-range can significantly reduce file sizes and improve performance. Variable fonts combine multiple weights and styles into a single file, reducing HTTP requests. Subsetting removes unused glyphs, and unicode-range allows the browser to download only needed character sets. This section checks for adoption of these modern optimization techniques.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the font analysis, this section provides actionable recommendations to optimize your typography stack. Each recommendation targets a specific area — from reducing file sizes with modern formats to improving layout stability with proper fallback chains. Implementing these changes can improve both performance metrics and user experience across all devices.

implementHttps.title: Implement HTTPS
implementHttps.summary: Your website is not using HTTPS encryption. All data including passwords, personal information, and payment details are transmitted in plain text, making them vulnerable to interception by attackers on the network.
steps: Obtain a free SSL certificate using certbot from Let's Encrypt
Install the certificate and configure your web server
Set up automatic HTTP→HTTPS redirect

implementCsp.title: Implement Content Security Policy
implementCsp.summary: Your site lacks a Content Security Policy (CSP) header, leaving it vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks. Attackers can inject malicious scripts that steal user data, hijack sessions, or deface your website.
steps: Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only header to identify issues
Set default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' as base policy
Replace inline scripts/styles with external files or add nonces
After testing, switch to Content-Security-Policy header for enforcement

enableHsts.title: Enable HTTP Strict Transport Security
enableHsts.summary: HSTS header is not configured. Without HSTS, attackers can perform protocol downgrade attacks, forcing users to connect over insecure HTTP even when HTTPS is available.
steps: First ensure HTTPS works on all pages
Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=300 to test
After testing, increase to max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains

preventClickjacking.title: Prevent Clickjacking Attacks
preventClickjacking.summary: X-Frame-Options header is not set. Attackers can embed your site in a hidden iframe and trick users into clicking buttons they didn't intend to, potentially changing settings or making purchases.
steps: Add X-Frame-Options: DENY header to your server config
Also add CSP: frame-ancestors 'none' for modern browsers

preventMimeSniffing.title: Prevent MIME Sniffing
preventMimeSniffing.summary: X-Content-Type-Options header is missing. Browsers may misinterpret file types, potentially executing uploaded files as scripts even if they have a different extension.
steps: Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header to all responses
Ensure your server sends correct Content-Type for all files
Test that file downloads and uploads still work correctly after implementation

improveCookieSecurity.title: Improve Cookie Security
improveCookieSecurity.summary: Cookies are not properly secured. Session cookies without HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags are vulnerable to theft via XSS attacks and cross-site request forgery.
steps: Add HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax flags to all session cookies
Update your session library or framework configuration
Test that login/logout functionality still works

addSri.title: Add Subresource Integrity
addSri.summary: Third-party scripts are loaded without integrity verification. If the CDN is compromised, malicious code could be injected into your site without detection.
steps: Generate SRI hashes for each external script/stylesheet at srihash.org
Add integrity and crossorigin="anonymous" attributes
Update hashes each time you upgrade library versions

sectionIntros.ssl: SSL/TLS certificates establish encrypted connections between your server and visitors, protecting data in transit. A valid, properly configured certificate is essential for user trust and search engine rankings. This section evaluates your certificate validity, protocol version, issuer, and expiration status. Modern sites should use TLS 1.2 or higher and ensure certificates are renewed well before expiration.
sectionIntros.headers: HTTP security headers provide an additional layer of protection against common web attacks like XSS, clickjacking, and MIME-type sniffing. These headers instruct browsers on how to handle your content securely. This section checks for six critical security headers recommended by OWASP. Implementing all recommended headers significantly reduces your attack surface.
sectionIntros.vulnerabilities: This section identifies potential security vulnerabilities detected during the analysis. Vulnerabilities are categorized by severity level from critical to low. Addressing critical and high-severity issues should be the top priority as they pose the greatest risk to your application and user data. Regular vulnerability assessments help maintain a strong security posture.
sectionIntros.cookies: Cookies store sensitive data like session tokens and user preferences. Improperly configured cookies can be intercepted, forged, or exploited through cross-site attacks. This section examines each cookie for security flags including HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite attributes. All cookies handling sensitive data should have these protective flags enabled.
sectionIntros.thirdParty: Third-party scripts introduce external code into your application, creating potential security risks. Each external script should be loaded with Subresource Integrity (SRI) to prevent tampering. This section audits all externally loaded scripts for SRI implementation, HTTPS usage, and loading method. Minimizing third-party dependencies and implementing SRI reduces your exposure to supply-chain attacks.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the security analysis, this section provides prioritized recommendations to strengthen your site's defenses. Each recommendation includes the severity level, potential impact, and actionable steps for implementation. Addressing critical and high-priority items first will provide the greatest improvement to your overall security posture.

sectionIntros.wcag: The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 define standards for making web content accessible to people with disabilities. Compliance is measured across four principles: Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, and Robust. This section evaluates your page against key WCAG Level AA success criteria. Meeting these standards ensures your site is usable by the widest possible audience and may be required by law in many jurisdictions.
sectionIntros.contrast: Sufficient color contrast ensures that text and interactive elements are readable by people with low vision or color vision deficiencies. WCAG 2.1 Level AA requires a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. This section identifies elements that fail to meet these thresholds. Fixing contrast issues is one of the most impactful accessibility improvements you can make.
sectionIntros.keyboard: Keyboard accessibility ensures that all interactive elements can be reached and operated using only a keyboard. This is essential for users who cannot use a mouse due to motor disabilities, as well as power users who prefer keyboard navigation. This section checks for focusable elements, tab traps, and visible focus indicators. Every interactive element must be reachable via Tab key and operable via Enter or Space.
sectionIntros.aria: ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes and semantic HTML provide the foundation for screen reader accessibility. Proper use of landmarks, labels, roles, and heading structure allows assistive technology to navigate and understand your page. This section checks for ARIA implementation quality, landmark regions, form labels, and heading hierarchy. Incorrect ARIA usage can actually make accessibility worse, so proper implementation is critical.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the accessibility audit, this section provides prioritized recommendations to improve your site's inclusivity. Each recommendation references the relevant WCAG success criterion and includes practical steps for implementation. Addressing high-priority items first will yield the greatest improvement in accessibility compliance and user experience for people with disabilities.

sectionIntros.cwv: Core Web Vitals are Google's key metrics for measuring real-world user experience. They assess loading speed (LCP), interactivity (INP/FID), and visual stability (CLS). These metrics directly influence search rankings through Google's page experience signals. This section presents your Core Web Vitals scores for both desktop and mobile, with performance ratings based on Google's published thresholds.
sectionIntros.lighthouse: Google Lighthouse provides automated auditing across four categories: Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, and SEO. Scores are calculated from dozens of individual audits weighted by impact. This section presents your Lighthouse scores for both desktop and mobile environments. Scores of 90+ are considered good, 50-89 need improvement, and below 50 are poor.
sectionIntros.resources: Resource analysis examines all assets loaded by your page, including JavaScript, CSS, images, and fonts. Excessive resources increase load times and bandwidth consumption. This section breaks down resource counts and sizes by type, helping identify optimization opportunities. Reducing unnecessary resources and optimizing asset delivery are among the most effective performance improvements.
sectionIntros.network: Network performance measures the speed of communication between the browser and your server. Time To First Byte (TTFB) is a critical indicator of server responsiveness. This section analyzes connection timing, DNS resolution, SSL negotiation, and DOM processing milestones. Optimizing server response times and connection setup directly improves the user experience for all visitors.
sectionIntros.caching: Effective caching reduces server load and dramatically improves page load times for returning visitors. Browser caching stores assets locally so they don't need to be re-downloaded on subsequent visits. This section evaluates your cache hit rate, cache control directives, and the proportion of cacheable resources. A well-configured caching strategy can reduce repeat-visit load times by 60-80%.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the performance analysis, this section provides actionable recommendations to improve your site's speed and user experience. Each recommendation includes the affected metric, current issue, and suggested solution. Prioritize high-impact items that affect Core Web Vitals, as these directly influence search rankings and user satisfaction.

sectionIntros.touch: Touch target sizing ensures interactive elements are easily tappable on touchscreen devices. Google recommends touch targets be at least 48x48 CSS pixels with adequate spacing. sectionIntros.readability: Mobile readability encompasses font sizing, line height, contrast, and text layout on small screens. Text that is too small, has poor contrast, or requires horizontal scrolling creates a poor reading experience. This section evaluates your content's readability across mobile viewport sizes.
sectionIntros.responsiveness: Responsive design ensures your layout adapts properly across different screen sizes and orientations. This section evaluates viewport configuration, media query usage, and layout behavior to identify issues that may cause content to overflow or display incorrectly on mobile devices.
sectionIntros.viewport: Viewport meta configuration and Progressive Web App (PWA) readiness determine how your site behaves on mobile devices. A properly configured viewport prevents unwanted zooming and scaling. PWA features like a web manifest and service worker enable app-like experiences.
sectionIntros.accessibility: Mobile accessibility focuses on ensuring your site is usable by people with disabilities on mobile devices. This includes touch target accessibility, screen reader compatibility, and gesture-based navigation support. Mobile-specific accessibility issues can affect a significant portion of your mobile audience.
sectionIntros.recommendations: Based on the mobile analysis, these recommendations target the most impactful improvements for mobile user experience, performance, and accessibility.

codeSnippet.defaultFallback:
Review and implement the GDPR compliance requirement.

Key considerations:
• Document your data processing activities
• Ensure lawful basis for processing
• Implement appropriate security measures
• Enable user rights (access, deletion, portability)
• Keep records of consent

dataSubjectRights.step1: Create a "Your Rights" page - Add a dedicated page explaining all GDPR rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction, objection)
dataSubjectRights.step2: Add request forms - Create online forms for each right type with clear submission process
dataSubjectRights.step3: Set up handling process - Define internal workflow for responding to requests within 30 days
dataSubjectRights.step4: Train your team - Ensure staff know how to verify identity and process different request types
dataSubjectRights.step5: Link prominently - Add links to rights page in footer, privacy policy, and account settings
dataSubjectRights.step6: Document everything - Keep records of all requests received and how they were handled

privacyContact.step1: Designate a DPO - Appoint a Data Protection Officer if required (public authority, large-scale processing, special categories)
privacyContact.step2: Create contact page - Add dedicated privacy contact section with email, phone, and postal address
privacyContact.step3: Set up privacy email - Create a dedicated privacy@yourcompany.com inbox monitored daily
privacyContact.step4: Define response SLA - Commit to responding to privacy inquiries within 48 hours
privacyContact.step5: Add to privacy policy - Include full contact details in your privacy policy header
privacyContact.step6: Provide escalation path - List supervisory authority contact for users who want to lodge complaints

consentWithdrawal.step1: Add cookie settings link - Provide a persistent "Cookie Settings" link in footer to re-open consent dialog
consentWithdrawal.step2: Email unsubscribe - Include one-click unsubscribe in all marketing emails (not just a preferences link)
consentWithdrawal.step3: Account settings - Add privacy preferences section in user account with toggle switches
consentWithdrawal.step4: Make it equally easy - GDPR requires withdrawal to be as easy as giving consent - no dark patterns
consentWithdrawal.step5: Process immediately - Withdrawal should take effect instantly, not "within 24 hours"
consentWithdrawal.step6: Keep consent records - Log when consent was given AND when it was withdrawn for compliance

dataRetention.step1: Audit your data - List all types of personal data you collect and where it's stored
dataRetention.step2: Define retention periods - Set specific timeframes for each data type based on legal/business need
dataRetention.step3: Document justification - Record why you need to keep data for the stated period
dataRetention.step4: Implement auto-deletion - Set up automated processes to delete data when retention expires
dataRetention.step5: Publish retention schedule - Add a clear table in your privacy policy showing all retention periods
dataRetention.step6: Review annually - Schedule yearly review of retention periods to ensure they're still justified

ageVerification.step1: Determine your age threshold - GDPR default is 16, but varies by country (UK: 13, Germany: 16, etc.)
ageVerification.step2: Add age gate - Implement age verification before account creation or data collection
ageVerification.step3: Parental consent flow - Create process for users under threshold to get parent/guardian approval
ageVerification.step4: Verify parental consent - Implement reasonable method to verify guardian identity
ageVerification.step5: Child-friendly language - If children can use your service, ensure privacy info is age-appropriate
ageVerification.step6: Special data protection - Minimize data collection from minors and never use for marketing

cookieConsent.step1: Choose a CMP - Select a GDPR-compliant Consent Management Platform (Cookiebot, OneTrust, etc.)
cookieConsent.step2: Scan your cookies - Audit all cookies set by your site and categorize them (essential, analytics, marketing)
cookieConsent.step3: Equal prominence - Show Accept and Reject buttons with equal visual weight - no dark patterns
cookieConsent.step4: Block until consent - Ensure non-essential cookies are blocked until explicit consent is given
cookieConsent.step5: Granular control - Allow users to accept/reject by category, not just all-or-nothing
cookieConsent.step6: Test thoroughly - Use browser DevTools to verify no cookies are set before consent

privacyPolicy.step1: Use a template - Start with a GDPR-compliant template and customize for your business
privacyPolicy.step2: Required disclosures - Include: data controller, DPO contact, data types, legal basis, retention, rights, transfers
privacyPolicy.step3: Plain language - Write in clear, understandable terms - avoid legal jargon where possible

addCaa.title: Add CAA DNS Records
addCaa.description: No CAA records found. CAA restricts which CAs can issue certificates for your domain.
addCaa.whyItMatters: CAA (Certificate Authority Authorization) records prevent unauthorized SSL certificate issuance. Without CAA, any CA can issue a certificate for your domain, potentially enabling man-in-the-middle attacks if a rogue certificate is issued.
technicalDetails: CAA records are DNS TXT records that specify which CAs can issue certificates
Major browsers and CAs now require checking CAA before certificate issuance
CAA helps protect against certificate misissuance attacks
Does not affect existing certificates, only future issuance

strengthenDmarc.title: Strengthen DMARC Policy
strengthenDmarc.description: Your DMARC policy is set to "none" (monitoring only).
strengthenDmarc.whyItMatters: Your DMARC policy is set to "none" which only monitors without blocking. Emails failing authentication still get delivered, making your domain vulnerable to spoofing attacks that damage brand reputation.
strengthenDmarc.impact: Low - Provides stronger email authentication enforcement
technicalDetails: DMARC policies: none (monitor) → quarantine (spam folder) → reject (block)
Aggregate reports (rua) show authentication statistics
Forensic reports (ruf) show individual failures
Gradual policy escalation prevents legitimate email disruption

implementDmarc.title: Implement DMARC Policy
implementDmarc.description: No DMARC record found. DMARC protects against email spoofing.
implementDmarc.whyItMatters: Without DMARC, attackers can easily spoof emails appearing to come from your domain. This enables phishing attacks against your customers, partners, and employees.
implementDmarc.impact: High - Protects brand reputation and prevents phishing
technicalDetails: DMARC builds on SPF and DKIM for complete email authentication
Provides visibility into who sends email on your behalf
Receiving servers use DMARC to decide how to handle unauthenticated emails
Major email providers (Gmail, Microsoft) increasingly require DMARC

configureSpf.title: Configure SPF Record
configureSpf.description: No valid SPF record found. SPF helps prevent email spoofing and improves deliverability.
configureSpf.whyItMatters: SPF (Sender Policy Framework) tells receiving servers which IPs are authorized to send email for your domain. Without it, spammers can send email pretending to be from your domain.
configureSpf.impact: High - Improves email deliverability and security
technicalDetails: SPF is a TXT record published in DNS
Lists authorized mail servers via IP or include mechanisms
Use ~all (soft fail) initially, then -all (hard fail) when confident
Maximum 10 DNS lookups allowed per SPF check

configureDkim.title: Configure DKIM
configureDkim.description: DKIM not configured. DKIM signs emails cryptographically to verify authenticity.
configureDkim.whyItMatters: DKIM cryptographically signs your emails, allowing recipients to verify the email came from your domain and wasn't modified in transit. This builds trust and improves deliverability.
configureDkim.impact: High - Improves email deliverability and authenticity
technicalDetails: DKIM uses public/private key cryptography
Private key signs outgoing emails on your mail server
Public key is published in DNS for verification
Key rotation recommended every 6-12 months

fixSslCertificate.title: Fix SSL Certificate
fixSslCertificate.description: SSL certificate issue detected. Certificate may be invalid, expired, or misconfigured.
fixSslCertificate.whyItMatters: An invalid SSL certificate causes browser security warnings that scare away visitors. It also prevents secure data transmission and hurts SEO rankings.
fixSslCertificate.impact: Critical - Fix immediately to restore trust and functionality
technicalDetails: SSL/TLS encrypts data between browser and server
Invalid certificates show security warnings to visitors
Search engines penalize sites with SSL issues
Free certificates available from Let's Encrypt

addNameservers.title: Add Additional Nameservers
addNameservers.description: Only one nameserver detected. This creates a single point of failure.
addNameservers.whyItMatters: Having only one nameserver means your entire domain becomes unreachable if that server goes down. DNS redundancy is essential for high availability.
technicalDetails: Minimum 2 nameservers recommended, 3-4 is better
Nameservers should be on different networks
Geographic distribution improves resilience
Most registrars provide multiple nameservers

renewCertificate.title: Renew SSL Certificate
renewCertificate.description: SSL certificate expires soon. Renew before expiration to avoid security warnings.
renewCertificate.whyItMatters: When your certificate expires, browsers will show security warnings preventing visitors from accessing your site. This can cause significant traffic and revenue loss.
technicalDetails: Most certificates valid for 1 year (some 90 days)
Set up auto-renewal if possible
Monitor expiration dates with alerting
Certificate installation requires server access

sectionIntros.issues: This section highlights implementation issues and conflicts found among your tags. sectionIntros.categories: Tags are organized by functional category to provide a clear picture of your marketing and analytics stack. sectionIntros.performance: Marketing tags and tracking scripts can significantly impact page load performance. Synchronous scripts block rendering while they load, and inline scripts add to the initial HTML payload. This section analyzes script loading methods, identifying blocking scripts that should be converted to async or defer loading. Optimizing script loading can reduce Time to Interactive by hundreds of milliseconds.
sectionIntros.thirdParty: Third-party scripts are loaded from external domains and include analytics libraries, advertising pixels, and CDN-hosted utilities. Each external script introduces a dependency on another server's availability and performance. This section catalogs all third-party scripts by host, category, and loading method. Minimizing third-party dependencies and ensuring proper async loading reduces performance risk.
sectionIntros.dataLayer: The dataLayer is a JavaScript array used by Google Tag Manager to pass structured data between your website and marketing tags. A well-implemented dataLayer centralizes event tracking and enables consistent measurement across all tags. This section checks for dataLayer presence, event count, and ecommerce implementation.
